goal: Show-me day: hook on whole seeds the children look at from the outside, the compelling question, and the teacher thinks aloud from looking to an "I wonder..." question, not a statement; the class wonder board begins
note: Show-me day with the skill card "look, wonder, say it" held by the teacher. The seeds stay whole today, so the inside is left to find: the teacher cuts one open on day 4. Each wonder goes on the board header cards (one board with social studies kindergarten unit 1, ssk-asking-questions, which runs the same weeks: science and social studies wonders go on it too). A child who prefers not to speak may point at a picture or whisper to the teacher. Case set neutral (APPROACH.md, Sensitive ground, item 1). No readiness check: kindergarten has no course before it and no row assumes one.

goal: Practice day: short repeated tries at saying an "I wonder" question about new pictures and objects, with feedback on question or statement; before a read-aloud, a guess from its cover about what the book holds
note: Seed picture set (Curio Class writes it). Candidate kept: the continuum's K cover-guess cell as one practice prompt before the seed read-aloud: the teacher shows one cover guess first, then children try; it stays about 3 minutes, no day added. Pairs hold the skill card. The teacher marks the class checklist by exception (question or statement). A child who prefers not to speak may point at a picture or whisper to the teacher.

goal: Show-me day: the cycle card's four pictures (ask, find, share, reflect), with the ask step run on one class question picked from the wonder board
note: The research-cycle model is met here first, as four pictured words. Host: a push-pull wonder from science kindergarten unit 1 (sk-push-pull, science days 1 to 9, weeks 1 to 5, in step) such as "why did the ball stop?"; stand-alone: "What is inside a seed?". ELA kindergarten meets the same cycle words later (ek-shared-research, ELA unit 3, weeks 16 to 24): bridge, this day teaches the four pictures itself, spoken and drawn, with no writing.

goal: Inquiry day: the class runs find and share on its question, listening to the seed read-aloud (with one seed the teacher cuts open as a second find source) or a visiting staff member, and each child draws one found fact with a label or a dictated sentence
note: Skill card withdrawn today (the first inquiry day). Seed read-aloud (Curio Class writes it); on the stand-alone path ("What is inside a seed?") the teacher cuts one seed open beside it, children only look. The drawing is the observed performance for the find and use steps of k-class-inquiry: the teacher marks the class checklist (one found fact, drawn and labeled or dictated) as children finish; this is an inquiry day, not a show-me day, so the frame's scoring rule holds. The visiting staff member (APPROACH.md, Sensitive ground, item 8): a neutral class topic, children's questions checked by the teacher first, no question about home or family. Candidate kept: the continuum's K connect cell (saying one or two new ideas from a read-aloud) as the share prompt on day 6, no day added. Drawings collected for the day 6 share circle. Whose voices: the unit records the makers of its read-aloud and pictures (C12).

goal: End-of-unit assessment, circle round on a picture not seen before: each child points at the four cycle pictures in order saying each step's word, then says one question about the picture
note: Circle round, about 30 seconds a child, about 15 minutes for 30, inside the 19 working minutes; no skill card. Two prompts a child: the cycle (k-class-inquiry; its checklist mark is the day 4 drawing plus this item, so the cycle is done, not only named) and the wonder (AASL.V.C.1, checklist: a question, not a statement). The teacher marks the class checklist. No warm-up on the scored move. Response time: day 6. A child who prefers not to speak may point at a picture or whisper to the teacher.

goal: Respond day: the share circle of the day 4 drawings, each child saying one thing a friend's drawing taught them, and the pointing self-check; then regrouped reteach by the step missed
note: Share circle and self-check about 10 minutes (point at the four pictures, say one step done well and one thing to do differently next time); then groups from the day 5 checklist, with a fresh try. Before the checklist is thrown away, the teacher writes the class count of each move (the day 4 find and draw, the day 5 items) on the mid-year check sheet. The checklist is thrown away at unit end (APPROACH.md, K to 2).

goal: Show-me day: hook on a pile of mixed books and the compelling question, "How do we find a book that answers our question, and look after it?"; then how the book corner works (clean hands, turning pages from the corner, a book back in its bin, borrowing and returning on a set day) and the stop rule as three pictured words on pretend picture cards
note: No opening retrieval today (four new routines; k-wonder returns on day 9). Skill card held by the teacher. Stop rule (close, tell, no blame) on the stop picture cards and a strip per child; no device and no real screen. The teacher page says what the adult does if an upsetting picture ever appears on a screen, and points to health's steps if a child tells something worrying (APPROACH.md, Sensitive ground, item 2). Sensitivity: borrowing is from the class book corner only, no book goes home unless the school's rules allow it, no child is asked about books at home, and a lost or damaged book is never a child's blame in front of the class. Outside guidance for the sensitivity read: the listing of a free K to 2 online-safety presentation (frame, Sensitivity reads); the kit itself is not loaded.

goal: Show-me day: the bins and their spine labels, and telling a story book from a fact book by the cover and a few pages
note: Opens with the five-minute retrieval task: point at the find picture on the cycle card and say what the class found it in. Bin label cards with picture or color dot stickers (reused all year); the room's own picture books. Candidate kept, no day added: the continuum's K cells that picture books can be true or not true (said at the sort) and that different tools in a library help find materials (the labels as the tool). Leans on ELA kindergarten unit 1 for the words "cover" and "title" (ek-books-and-authors, ELA days 1 to 34, weeks 1 to 7, before this day).

goal: Practice day: fetch a book from a named bin and put it back in the bin it lives in, sort a small pile into story books and fact books, and point along the stop strip; then the class borrowing choice
note: Opens with the five-minute retrieval task: one "I wonder" about a new picture. Pairs hold the skill card "look at the label, find the bin, bring it back". Story-or-fact sort set (Curio Class writes it). Candidate kept as a borrowing-day choice, not a scored skill: each child picks a book of their own interest from the corner, about 3 minutes. Space: one pair at a bin at a time, the rest on the carpet.

goal: Inquiry day on the rain question: find the labeled bin, pick the fact book over the story book with help, listen to a short rain passage, and each child draws one fact that helps answer it (the partner share opens day 12)
note: Skill card withdrawn today (the first inquiry day). Opens with the cycle card held up for this one day (unit 2's run of the whole cycle, the day's own skill, not a retrieval), then on the wall. Find-step prompt: "Which bin holds the rain book?". Judge at K depth is the fact-book pick. Host: a fact book about weather from ELA kindergarten unit 2 (ELA days 35 to 76, weeks 7 to 16, in step), or the weather watch of science kindergarten unit 2 (sk-weather-watch, weeks 5 to 9, taught just before); stand-alone: "What happens when rain falls?" with the rain read-aloud. The day ends at the drawing; the partner share and the pointing self-check open day 12.

goal: End-of-unit assessment: at a station of five, each child brings back a book from a named bin not used in practice, says story book or fact book, answers "Which one would help us find out about ___?" for a named question, and puts it back; then the whole circle points along the stop strip as the teacher describes an upsetting picture
note: About 17 minutes for 30: six station groups of five at about 2.5 minutes, while the others do the practiced story-or-fact sort in the book corner; then the stop strip scanned across the circle in about 2 minutes. The described picture stays mild and pretend (a scary cartoon face), never a real image. Each prompt asks one part of each row: fetch, sort, which one would help (the ~AASL.IV.A.2 slice, a few seconds a child), put back; close, tell, no blame. No skill card. Response time: day 12.

goal: Respond day: partner shares of the rain drawings and the pointing self-check, then regrouped reteach by the step missed on the fetch, the sort or the stop strip
note: Shares and self-check about 10 minutes, then groups from the day 11 checklist with a fresh try. Before the checklist is thrown away, the teacher writes a class count of the children who met each move on the mid-year check sheet (reused unscored on day 13; no per-child record outlives the unit).

goal: Mid-year check, circle round on a picture not seen before: each child points at the four cycle pictures in order saying each step's word, and says one "I wonder" question about the picture; it samples unit 1 on a new case, not unit 2
note: About 30 seconds a child, about 15 minutes for 30. Unit 2, just assessed on day 11, is not re-tested: its class count from day 12 is copied onto this sheet unscored (sequence-write rule 3). The circle-round form was last used on day 5 (week 5), so no form repeats within two weeks. No opening retrieval of the scored moves. A child who prefers not to speak may point at a picture or whisper to the teacher.

goal: Mid-year respond day: small groups reteach the cycle step or the wonder each child missed, from the check sheet, each ending with one fresh try
note: Groups from the day 13 sheet; the rest of the class at a practiced book-corner task. No readiness check before unit 3: its row assumes nothing.

goal: Show-me day: hook on the rabbit question (the unit's question, answered on day 17), then the teacher models the move on a parallel case: the teacher holds "What does a tortoise eat?" aloud while reading a tortoise passage and stops at the sentence that answers it, retelling that one fact
note: Opens with the five-minute retrieval task: fetch the fact-book bin by its label. Skill card "hold the question, listen, hand up, say it" held by the teacher. Tortoise model passage (Curio Class writes it); the rabbit read-aloud is not read today, so the inquiry on day 17 keeps something to find. Sensitivity: the case set keeps to plant eaters, so no passage describes a hunt. Case set neutral (APPROACH.md, Sensitive ground, item 1).

goal: Practice day: three short read-aloud passages about other plant eaters, each with one held question; hands up at the answering sentence and the fact retold in the child's own words, with feedback
note: Opens with the five-minute retrieval task: put a book back in the bin it lives in and say why. Three short passages about other plant eaters, not the rabbit or the day 15 tortoise (Curio Class writes them). Pairs hold the skill card. Candidate dropped: telling the main idea of a read-aloud is ELA's (STANDARD.md section 4) and pulls the other way from this unit's move (the part that answers, not every part).

goal: Inquiry day: the class asks its animal question from the board, listens for the answer in the rabbit read-aloud, read for the first time today, and each child draws the answering fact
note: Skill card withdrawn today (the first inquiry day). Opens with the cycle card held up for this one day (the day's own skill, not a retrieval), then on the wall. Host: what an animal needs and where it lives, sk-needs-places in science kindergarten unit 4 (science days 32 to 43, weeks 15 to 20, in step), or the ELA trees research when it is running (ek-shared-research, ELA unit 3 from week 16); stand-alone: "What does a rabbit eat?". Candidate kept, no day added: taking notes on facts by drawing them (the continuum's K cell) is the drawing itself. Whose voices: the unit records the makers of its passages (C12).

goal: End-of-unit assessment, whisper walk: the teacher names a held question and reads once a short passage not heard before about a different plant eater, then each child whispers the fact that answers it
note: About 2 minutes to read, then about 15 seconds a child, about 10 minutes for 30, so no child repeats a neighbor; the rest of the session is the practiced book-corner task. No skill card. Response time: day 19.

goal: Respond day: the class share circle of the day 17 drawings and the pointing self-check, then regrouped reteach on holding the question and the answering sentence
note: Share circle and self-check about 10 minutes, then groups from the day 18 checklist with a fresh try on a fresh-try passage (another plant eater). No readiness check before unit 4: its rows assume nothing.

goal: Show-me day: hook on the tree question, then the talking object and the group turn of three: each child tells one fact while the others listen, and the group says what each friend added
note: Opens with the five-minute retrieval task: hold a question and raise a hand at the answer in a two-sentence passage. Skill card "eyes look, wait my turn, what did Sam add, who made it" held by the teacher: it opens with the two pictures of SEL's talk turn card in SEL's words (SEL STANDARD section 7), then adds library's steps. Where the school runs SEL, the class already knows the first two pictures; where it does not, this day teaches them. Talking object: anything the room has. The class's talk rules from social studies kindergarten (ssk-talk-together, weeks 3 to 4 and again in week 23) and ELA (ek-discussion) are used where they exist; this day teaches the turn itself otherwise. Candidate kept, no day added: listening and raising a hand before speaking, folded into the talking-object turn. Groups mixed by the teacher, never by background. A child who prefers not to speak may point at a picture or whisper to the teacher.

goal: Show-me day: before and after a read-aloud, who wrote the words and who made the pictures, pointing to the names on the cover; a person made this book, so a found fact came from its maker and an idea of one's own is one's own
note: Opens with the five-minute retrieval task: say story book or fact book from a cover. Leans on ELA kindergarten unit 1 (ek-books-and-authors, weeks 1 to 7, before this day): the words author and illustrator are retrieved there; if a class has not had ELA, this day teaches them itself. Honest use without shaming (APPROACH.md, Sensitive ground, item 4): a child who calls a found fact "mine" is helped to say "I found it in...", never corrected in front of the group.

goal: Practice day: group turns with the talking object on a new picture set, then each group points to the maker's name on its cover card and says who made it
note: Opens with the five-minute retrieval task: one "I wonder" about the picture set. Tree picture set 1 and cover cards (Curio Class writes them). Groups hold the skill card. Space: groups of three spread round the carpet edge, one cover card a group.

goal: Inquiry day: the class asks its tree question, and each group finds facts in its picture set and the tree read-aloud, each child drawing one fact and the group naming the book's maker
note: Skill card withdrawn today (the first inquiry day). Opens with the cycle card held up for this one day (the day's own skill, not a retrieval), then on the wall. Tree read-aloud and tree picture sets 2 and 3. Host: the trees research of ELA kindergarten unit 3 (ek-shared-research, in step: ELA days 80 to 118, weeks 16 to 24; the class brings its ELA tree facts in as found facts); stand-alone: "What lives in and around a tree?". Whose voices: the unit records the makers of its read-aloud and pictures (C12).

goal: Inquiry day: the group share in the circle, each group saying "We found that... in the book by...", with each child telling their fact; then the class says what feedback is and how a friend's words helped
note: The year's last product: the group drawings shared in the circle. Candidate kept, no day added: the continuum's K cells on what feedback is and why it helps, about 3 minutes after the shares. A child who prefers not to speak hands the talking object on and points at their fact.

goal: End-of-unit assessment: groups of three at the check table with a picture set not seen before, each child telling one fact in turn and saying what one friend added; then each pair points to the maker's name on its cover card
note: About 17 minutes for 30: ten groups at about 1.5 minutes while the others do a practiced book-corner task, then the cover-card pointing scanned across the circle in about 2 minutes. Prompts: tell one fact, say what a friend added, point to the maker. No skill card. Response time: day 26.

goal: Respond day: the pointing self-check on the group share, then regrouped reteach on the turn, the friend's addition or the maker's name
note: Self-check about 5 minutes, then groups from the day 25 checklist with a fresh try. Before the checklist is thrown away, the teacher writes the class count of each move on the year-end check sheet (reused unscored on days 27 and 28).

goal: Year-end check, session 1, whisper walk: a held question and a passage not heard before about another plant eater, read once; each child whispers the fact that answers it and one "I wonder" about the passage's animal; it samples units 1 and 3, not unit 4
note: About 2 minutes to read, then about 25 seconds a child, about 15 minutes for 30. Unit 4, just assessed on day 25, is reused unscored as its class count (sequence-write rule 3). Last whisper walk: day 18, week 18.

goal: Year-end check, session 2, at a station of five: each child brings back a book from a named bin, says story book or fact book, answers "Which one would help us find out about ___?" for a named question, and puts it back in its bin; it samples unit 2 on new bins and books
note: The which-one prompt asks the ~AASL.IV.A.2 slice, a few seconds a child. About 2.5 minutes a group, six groups, about 15 minutes for 30, while the others do the practiced story-or-fact sort. Two forms need two sessions: each fills about 15 of the 19 working minutes. Last station form: day 11, week 11.

goal: Year-end respond day 1: small groups reteach the gaps from the check sheet (the answering fact, the wonder, the fetch, sort and put back), each ending with a fresh try
note: Groups from the days 27 and 28 sheet; the rest at a practiced book-corner task.

goal: Year-end respond day 2, the year's reflect step: the class looks back over its wonder board, and each child says one wonder they still have and one cycle step they now do well
note: The continuum's PK to 2 reflect skills and the self-check, taken for the year. The teacher takes a last try with any child the reteach did not reach. The teacher passes the grade 1 teacher a class-level note of the moves the class needs again, never a per-child record.
